title: Assay result
description:
One sample's laboratory results: a row per sample carrying its analyte values in `elements[]`, each traceable to the method and certificate that produced it.

GENERATED from the normative OpenAPI document (`spec/openapi.yaml`) — do not edit by hand; run `python scripts/regenerate.py`. The OpenAPI document is normative for the wire; this file is the same contract for one record type, readable on its own.
x-generated-by: scripts/regenerate.py from spec/openapi.yaml (geoDB Open Exploration Protocol v0.3.2)

project.description: The project this assay belongs to, as an identity object rather than a bare id, so a reference stays meaningful across exports.

certificate.description: The lab job that created this row, as an identity object. On a merged row (one sample, two labs) the values may come from a different job — read the per-value `elements[].certificate` for provenance. Sent only with `expand=certificate`; otherwise `certificate_id` names it.

detection_limit_per_sample.description: Per-sample detection limit reported by the lab when a method has variable DL (Method.is_floating_dl=True). For BDL rows the AssayUnit stores value=-1 and this field carries the lab's reported '<X.XX' threshold.

precision_per_sample.description: Per-sample analytical precision (1-sigma error) reported by the lab. Drives the strip-log error whisker on the Au track for photon-assay samples. NULL for fixed-DL methods that only report a method-level precision.

analyte_mass_g.description: Actual sample mass loaded by the lab in grams. Distinct from the cutsheet's target mass — the lab reports what it really put on the instrument. Drives per-sample DL scaling on the photon-assay strip-log render.

lab_status_code.description:
Lab QC flag for this sample. BDL = below detection limit; HB / HET = heterogeneity flagged by lab (soft-warn, row imports normally); IS = insufficient sample (AssayUnit lands with value NULL); SNR = sample not received. Empty for samples with no flag.

* `BDL` - Below Detection Limit
* `HB` - Heterogeneity bias flagged by lab
* `HET` - Heterogeneous
* `IS` - Insufficient sample
* `SNR` - Sample not received

oneOf.description:
* `BDL` - Below Detection Limit
* `HB` - Heterogeneity bias flagged by lab
* `HET` - Heterogeneous
* `IS` - Insufficient sample
* `SNR` - Sample not received

value.description: The analyte value, as a DECIMAL STRING rather than a JSON number, stored and sent at 4 decimal places (a value the laboratory reported with more was rounded to 4 when it was loaded); parsing it as a float may round it again. Parse it with a decimal type. Its units are the sibling `units` field: units are per VALUE, not per sample and not per element, because one sample can carry values from two laboratories at different units. ⚠️ A below-detection result is stored and sent as the sentinel `-1.0000` (and flagged `below_detection: true` where the value carries that flag) — a marker, never a measurement or a grade. Compare it NUMERICALLY (a negative value is below detection), never as text: "-1", "-1.0" and "-1.0000" are the same value. The lab's threshold for that sample is `detection_limit_per_sample` when the method reports one, else the method's `detection_limit`.

units.description: Units for this value (e.g. `ppm`, `ppb`, `pct`, `g/t`, `oz/ton`). Per value — always read it beside the value rather than assuming a project-wide unit.

detection_limit.description: A method limit in the value's own units, or null when the method declares none. A float, unlike `value`, which is a decimal string because it is what the laboratory reported.

upper_limit.description: A method limit in the value's own units, or null when the method declares none. A float, unlike `value`, which is a decimal string because it is what the laboratory reported.

above_det_limit.description: True when the laboratory reported this value OVER its upper reporting limit (e.g. `>10000`): `value` is then the limit and the true value is AT LEAST that much. It does NOT mean "above the detection limit" — a below-detection result is the `-1.0000` sentinel, flagged by `below_detection`.

method.description: The analytical method that produced this value, as an identity object. `is_floating_dl` says whether the detection limit is reported per sample rather than fixed by the method. Sent only with `expand=method`; otherwise `method_id` names it.

certificate.description: The lab job that produced THIS value. Differs from the row's certificate on a merged row; null when the value carries no stamp of its own and the row's job could not be resolved. Sent only with `expand=certificate`; otherwise `certificate_id` names it.

below_detection.description: True when the laboratory reported this value BELOW its detection limit. `value` then holds the sentinel `-1.0000`, which is a marker, never a grade: the threshold is `detection_limit` (`detection_limit_per_sample` on the assay row for a method that reports one per sample). geoDB stores the sentinel and substitutes only when it MERGES values (half the detection limit by default, per the project's merge settings) — do not substitute twice.

certificate_id.description: Id of the certificate (laboratory job) that produced THIS value — the same job as `certificate.id`, flat. Null when the value carries no provenance of its own and the row's job could not be resolved.

items.description: What is wrong with a stored row. geoDB returns stored data as it is; this marks it so it can be found and corrected.

code.description: `above_upper_limit_as_value`: an assay value is above its method's upper limit but is stored as a plain number, not flagged over range (">UL"); the true value is unknown, at least the limit — look for a re-assay by an ore-grade method.; `azimuth_out_of_range`: azimuth (or dip direction) is outside 0..360 degrees.; `below_detection_limit_as_value`: an assay value is below its method's detection limit but is stored as a plain number, not as a below-detection result ("<DL"); treat it as below detection.; `coordinate_outside_crs`: the coordinate cannot be in its epsg (degrees beyond ±90 latitude or ±180 longitude under EPSG:4326).; `crs_implausible`: the coordinate looks like degrees of longitude/latitude but its epsg is a projected system in metres or feet, so it sits near that grid's origin (often at the equator on a map).; `depth_past_hole`: the depth lies beyond the hole's total depth.; `dip_out_of_range`: dip is outside -90..90 degrees.; `interval_upside_down`: depth_from is greater than depth_to (an upside-down interval).; `invalid_geometry`: the stored geometry is not valid (for example a self-intersecting outline).; `missing_epsg`: the record has coordinates but no epsg, so their CRS is unknown.; `negative_value`: a depth, length or total depth is negative.; `sample_trashed`: the assay's sample is in the trash; the assay is kept (never deleted with its sample) and re-links if the sample is restored or re-imported — leave it out of statistics unless told otherwise.

field.description: The field the warning is about.

data_warnings.description: Present only when this stored row has a problem geoDB can recognise (an upside-down interval, a dip past 90°, coordinates with no CRS…). The row is returned exactly as stored — never fixed or hidden; correct it with an update.

excluded.description: True when a QAQC review WITHHOLDS this row from results by default: it is returned only so you can explain why it is missing. Never average, plot or report a flagged row as a result.

excluded_reason.description: Why the row is withheld, or null when it is not. `certificate_rejected`: its certificate failed QAQC review. `certificate_superseded`: its certificate was replaced by a re-assay — read `superseded_by` on the certificate for the job that carries the live values. `certificate_pending_approval`: the project requires QAQC approval before results are used and this certificate's review is still pending.

excluded_by_certificate.description: The certificate whose review withholds this row — name it when you explain the gap. Usually the row's own certificate; on a merged row it can be the rejected job that produced the values. Null when the row is not withheld.

source_type.description: `lab` — laboratory results. `field_xrf` — a portable-XRF reading (field guidance, never a reportable grade; left out of lab analytics, QC and intercepts by default).

project_id.description: The project this record is in (a credential may read several; GET /api/v2/grant-context/ names them).

sample_status.description: `trashed`: the assay's sample is in the Trash — the assay is kept and re-links on restore; a list leaves such assays out unless `include_trashed_samples=true`, a read by id returns it. Leave it out of statistics.
